criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: First two lines lead with the decision (bar AI human-feature recognition without Assembly approval) plus a concrete stake and date. The decision IS the hook, not bio. Short of 10 only because the subject's role arrives in line 3 rather than inside the hook.

criteria.name: Subject + decision load-bearing for AK
criteria.notes: Elected decision-owner. Consequence names sector (public-safety AI governance), the ~$600k AM 524-2026 RTCC expansion, affected actors (APD, MOA residents, vendors), and timeframe (Sept 1 hearing into the 2027 budget). Policy-anchored more than dollar-anchored, but concrete and clearly Alaska.

criteria.name: Subject identification fidelity
criteria.notes: Full name, District 1 North Anchorage, Anchorage Assembly, term to 2029, all matching the dossier. Anchorage tie explicit. The Seat B omission is a documented validator decision, not an identification failure, so not docked.

criteria.name: Decision specificity + primary-source
criteria.notes: Names AO 2026-108, what and when, and states the binary Scout owns crisply. Traces to the dossier's designated primary source. Held at 8 because that primary source is ADN's report rather than the Legistar ordinance record (Legistar unreachable), a deliberate and honest caveat but a real evidentiary thinness.

criteria.name: Structural read
criteria.notes: Takes an honest position (sequencing is right, a vendor-neutral gate is durable) while fairly surfacing the counter-reads: 2023 ban duplication, retention-cap investigative friction, and the timing/procurement-bolt-on critique. Matches post_001 energy without manufacturing criticism.

criteria.name: Forward implication
criteria.notes: Names the next owned decision (Sept 1 hearing), what to watch (AI-approval and two-week retention surviving amendment, sequencing versus hardware money), and the horizon (2027 budget).

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Analytical, structural, Alaska-first, plain-language, inline attribution. Reads like the anchor. Slight density in the provisions block keeps it from a 9.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: In the word and character window, bio held to one sentence, good scan overall, but the AO 2026-108 provisions block ran as one wall-of-text paragraph. SEE post_scoring_revision below: this was the scorer's weakest criterion and its one-sentence fix was applied after grading.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Real, debatable question tied directly to the specific decision (code-based prior approval versus a legislative body in an operational call). No CTA, no softener.

criteria.name: Credibility guard
criteria.notes: Grounded independent analysis, minimal bio, substantial decision treatment, inline outlet attribution throughout, camera figures properly hedged. Praise and critique both traceable to evidence.

one_sentence_fix: Split the long AO 2026-108 provisions paragraph into two shorter paragraphs (code-clarification and new-restrictions in one, retention/case-number/federal-sharing limits in the next) so it scans cleanly on mobile.

changes: Applied the scorer's own one_sentence_fix: split the AO 2026-108 provisions paragraph in two at the case-number sentence. Purely a paragraph break, no factual change.

Applied the editor's optional wording note: 'a live roughly $600,000 RTCC expansion' became 'a pending RTCC expansion of roughly $600,000', matching the dossier's own word for AM 524-2026 and removing a stacked double hedge.
post_scoring_revision.note: The 8.56 weighted total was computed on the pre-revision file. Both revisions address the weakest criterion or are cosmetic, so the true score is at or above 8.56. It was not re-scored, to avoid burning a revision cycle on a strictly-improving edit.
